title: The matching scheme of a termwise fibre product is the fibre product of the matching schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $U_\bullet\to X$, $V_\bullet\to X$ be augmented simplicial $X$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. Let $W_\bullet\to X$ be the augmented simplicial $X$-scheme with $W_n=U_n\times_XV_n$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of the structure morphisms to $X$), whose face and degeneracy maps are the induced morphisms $d_i\times_{\mathrm{id}_X}d_i$, $s_i\times_{\mathrm{id}_X}s_i$ and whose augmentation is the structure morphism $W_0\to X$, and let $p:W_\bullet\to U_\bullet$, $q:W_\bullet\to V_\bullet$ be the termwise projections. For $n\geq0$ write $M_n(-)$ for the matching scheme of [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]: $M_0(-)=X$, and for $n\geq1$ the limit, in schemes over $X$, of the diagram formed by the terms in degrees $k<n$ indexed by the injective non-identity order-preserving maps $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ (with the simplicial operators between them), and write $\mu_n^U:U_n\to M_n(U)$ for the matching map whose $\delta$-component is the simplicial operator of $\delta$ (for $n=0$ the augmentation). Then for every $n\geq0$ the morphism $(M_n(p),M_n(q)):M_n(W)\to M_n(U)\times_XM_n(V)$ induced by $p$ and $q$ is an isomorphism, and under it $\mu_n^W$ corresponds to the induced morphism $\mu_n^U\times_{\mathrm{id}_X}\mu_n^V:U_n\times_XV_n\to M_n(U)\times_XM_n(V)$.

proof.text: For $n=0$, the matching scheme of each augmented object is $X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. Either projection $X\times_XX\to X$ is inverse to the unique map $X\to X\times_XX$ induced by $(\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_X)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under this identification the induced map from $W_0=U_0\times_XV_0$ is the pair of the two augmentations, namely $\mu_0^U\times_{\mathrm{id}_X}\mu_0^V$.

source.place: Lemma 018D (lemma-cosk-fibre-product), degree-zero case, expanded from the omitted proof; Hypercoverings Lemma 01GH (lemma-funny-gamma), proof

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$, and let $D_n$ be the finite boundary indexing category in the statement. For a test $X$-scheme $T$, a cone from $T$ to the diagram $\delta\mapsto W_k=U_k\times_XV_k$ consists of maps $c^W_\delta:T\to W_k$ compatible with every arrow of $D_n$. Taking the two projections gives cones $(c^U_\delta)$ and $(c^V_\delta)$ to the boundary diagrams of $U$ and $V$: the diagram maps of $W$ are induced by the corresponding diagram maps of $U$ and $V$ [def-pc-fibre-product], so all compatibility equations hold after projection. Conversely, given those two cones, for every $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ the pair $(c^U_\delta,c^V_\delta)$ has the same composite to $X$, because both are morphisms over $X$, and therefore defines a unique $c^W_\delta:T\to U_k\times_XV_k$. For each arrow of $D_n$, the required equation between the $c^W_\delta$ holds after both projections by compatibility of the two given cones; hence it holds by uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. These two constructions are inverse and natural in $T$.

source.place: Lemma 018D (lemma-cosk-fibre-product), omitted proof, expanded using the hom-set argument of Lemma 018C (lemma-cosk-product)

proof.text: By the limit property in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], maps $T\to M_n(W)$ are exactly cones of the first kind in step 2, while maps $T\to M_n(U)$ and $T\to M_n(V)$ are exactly the two cones of the second kind. By [def-pc-fibre-product], maps $T\to M_n(U)\times_XM_n(V)$ are exactly pairs of the latter cones (their maps to $X$ agree since $T$ and all boundary terms lie over $X$). The natural inverse correspondence of step 2 thus produces inverse morphisms between these matching schemes: apply it to the identity map of each matching scheme, then use its naturality to see both composites act as the identity on every map from a test $T$. The forward morphism is $(M_n(p),M_n(q))$, since its two projected boundary cones are precisely those obtained from the simplicial projections $p,q$. Hence this is the claimed isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 018D (lemma-cosk-fibre-product), universal-property proof omitted there; compare Lemma 018C (lemma-cosk-product), displayed hom-set calculation

proof.text: For each boundary index $\delta:[k]\to[n]$, the $\delta$-component of the cone defining $\mu_n^W:W_n\to M_n(W)$ is the simplicial operator $W_n\to W_k$, which by the definition of $W$ is the induced product of $U_n\to U_k$ and $V_n\to V_k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Projecting this cone gives exactly the boundary cones defining $\mu_n^U\circ p_n$ and $\mu_n^V\circ q_n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. Thus the isomorphism of step 3 sends $\mu_n^W$ to the unique morphism into $M_n(U)\times_XM_n(V)$ with these two projections, namely $\mu_n^U\times_{\mathrm{id}_X}\mu_n^V$; uniqueness follows from [def-pc-fibre-product]. Together with step 1 this proves the compatibility for all $n\geq0$.
